label: Metrically finite past of a moment
definition: MetricallyFinitePast k t holds when the clock readings of the moments at or before t are bounded below (Mathlib BddBelow of the image of Set.Iic t): the past of t has finite duration. Its negation is a metrically infinite past. Examples: in the positive reals (0, infinity) and the non-negative reals [0, infinity) every past is metrically finite, whether or not there is a first moment; in the integers or the full real line none is. In linear time a past with a beginning is metrically finite (metricallyFiniteOfBegun); the converse fails in the positive reals, whose pasts are finite but have no first moment.
note: Analyst metric definition; attribution deferred. It is relative to the supplied TimeClock and not invariant under reparametrization (CLOCK disambiguation 725f3417-73d0-489f-b8ab-7b2628ff36b7): arctan makes every integer past finite, ln t makes every positive real past infinite; the intended reading uses the privileged clock (CLOCK_1). A real clock exists only for orders embedding in the reals, so pasts with no countable coinitial subset are outside its scope. It is distinct from BegunAt (a minimal moment, an order notion) and from Acc (no endless descent, an order notion): an open-below finite past, as in standard FLRW cosmology, is metrically finite, beginningless and not founded.
